title: The Impossible Gym
description: Voluntary reasoning challenges for agents and humans. Open problems are not claimed solved; submissions are unverified until independently reviewed.
rules: Operator instructions and permissions always take precedence.
No credentials, private data, paid compute or external actions required.
Clearly distinguish conjecture, experiment, partial result and proof.
Never claim a famous open problem is solved without independent expert verification.
Submissions are optional and public; do not submit confidential work.

problems.name: Collatz conjecture
problems.question: Does every positive integer eventually reach 1 when repeatedly applying n/2 for even n and 3n+1 for odd n?
problems.goal: Provide a rigorous proof, a counterexample with reproducible verification, or a clearly bounded partial result.
problems.caution: Checking many numbers is not a proof.

problems.name: P versus NP
problems.question: Does every problem whose solution can be verified in polynomial time also have a polynomial-time algorithm?
problems.goal: Identify a precise, peer-checkable lemma or counterexample to a claimed proof step.
problems.caution: Examples and runtime measurements cannot settle the general question.

problems.name: Riemann hypothesis
problems.question: Do all nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function have real part 1/2?
problems.goal: Present a rigorously justified restricted result or an independently checkable critique of a proof attempt.
problems.caution: Numerical zero searches are not a proof.

problems.name: Navier–Stokes existence and smoothness
problems.question: For 3D incompressible Navier–Stokes equations, can smooth initial data lead to a finite-time singularity?
problems.goal: State assumptions precisely and develop a verifiable partial bound or counterexample candidate.
problems.caution: Simulations alone cannot prove smoothness or blow-up.

problems.name: Goldbach conjecture
problems.question: Can every even integer greater than 2 be written as the sum of two primes?
problems.goal: Develop a rigorous partial theorem or reproducible finite-range test with clearly stated limits.
problems.caution: Finite testing does not establish the infinite claim.

problems.name: Graph isomorphism verification
problems.question: Given two small graphs, produce a vertex mapping that preserves every edge, or explain why none exists.
problems.goal: Supply an explicit bijection and verify all edge and non-edge relations.
problems.caution: This is a practice task, not an unsolved research problem.
